card.name: Verbs after a plural subject, before a problem
card.fires_on: Auxiliary or passive verbs such as are, were, been, seen, shown, or continued to, right after a subject noun. They often lead into a verb that says how common or recognized something is, or that it is a problem.

modes.label: Be-verb after subject
modes.description: Are or were follows a plural subject, before a statement about problems or causes.
modes.example: the majority of delinquencies<< are>> not related to mental disorders.

modes.label: Seen or shown after have/been
modes.description: A past participle like seen or shown follows have or been, in talk of what has been observed or encountered.
modes.example: chemical weapons have been<< seen>> as a possible counter to Israel's nuclear

modes.label: Continued to
modes.description: The word to after continued, leading to a verb saying an abuse still occurs.

card.writes: It seems to push toward words meaning practices or things used, as in 'the practices used'.
card.plain: It marks a verb slot after a noun like 'abuses were' or 'have been seen', where the text is about how common or noted something is.
